text:
mira: FYI seeing a consistent ~12-18% unexplained peak GPU memory delta on 8x A100 inference runs vs the single-GPU baseline. NVPROF / CUPTI traces point at NCCL staging + lots of ephemeral temp allocs around the TP-gather and attention kernels.

mira: profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
[pid  1234] cudaMalloc  14.3 MB  (temp)  // kernel workspace
[pid  1234] cudaMalloc  256 MB  // nccl comm staging chunk
[pid  1234] cudaFree    14.3 MB
peak_rss: 39.6 GB  (expected 34.2 GB)
```

dave: model + batch shape? is kv-cache on for these runs?

mira: model=redwood-34b-fp16, kv-cache enabled, tokens per request skewed (many short + few long -> batching heuristics create weird seqlen mixes). batch shape is dynamic, effective micro-batch per GPU ~2-4.

kyle: two suspicions: 1) NCCL internal chunking + rendezvous pushes an extra buffer per peer when tensor-parallel shards are gathered, 2) allocator fragmentation from repeated small temp allocations (kernels ask/free every step). both can add up.

ana: +1. also kernel selection fallback can pick a path that needs larger workspace (e.g., fused-attn fallback -> big temp). did you capture which kernels had the big cudaMallocs?

mira: traced kernel names: fused_attn_bwd_v2, kv_gather_shard, tp_allgather_impl. The big 256MB shows up tied to NCCL send/recv staging in the same timeline.

kyle: quick mitigations to try:
- pre-allocate a shared NCCL comm pool on startup and set NCCL_BUFFSIZE / NCCL_SPLIT to smaller chunks to avoid per-op big allocs.
- switch allocator to carving slab for temp workspaces (size classes 8MB/16MB/64MB/256MB) and enable reuse across kernels.
- change batching heuristic to group by seq_len bucket more aggressively so TP shards don't create heavy stragglers.

mira: can we safely pre-allocate NCCL staging? iirc NCCL will still allocate its temp buffers per-launch unless we intercept at runtime and provide pinned buffer via comm plugin.

ana: we can: two approaches — (A) allocate a pinned host/device staging area and export pointer to our comm wrapper so we reuse it for every collective. (B) reduce NCCL chunk size (NCCL_BUFFSIZE) so it doesn't request huge contiguous allocation. both are doable. (A) better for fragmentation.

dave: let's be careful with pinned host memory size (PCIe pinned limits on some instances). prefer device-side prealloc pool with a fallback to host if device pool exhausted.

infra-bot: scheduled perf-matrix job perf/1843 on cluster-dedicated-8xA100 (batch: mixed, kv:on, with/without-commpool). ETA 2h :gear:

kyle: experimental plan:
1) baseline (current master)
2) + allocator slab reuse (dev branch alloc-slab)
3) + comm prealloc pool (dev branch comm-pool)
4) + batching tweak (bucketed batcher)
For each run capture: peak GPU RSS, nvprof timeline, and allocator free/alloc counts.

mira: I'll attach the perf traces here once infra-bot finishes. if slab reuse knocks down the repeated small cudaMallocs we should see the peak converge ~5-8% lower. if comm-pool reduces the 256MB spikes, we might reclaim another ~6-10%.

ana: also add a run that forces the alternative kernel path (smaller workspace) via kernel hint env var, to ensure kernel selection is also part of the equation. we should measure both workspace and execution time (no regressions).

dave: question: does KV-cache growth cause fragmentation? we reassign KV buffers on sequence length changes, could be freeing into different size classes. maybe pin KV cache per-shard and use a lazy grow with memcpy instead of free/alloc churn.

kyle: yeah — proposal: keep a persistent kv slab per-device sized to 1.2x observed max for the customer workload, and only fallback to dynamic alloc if exceeded. add an eviction policy for long-unused keys.

mira: action items:
- infra-bot run completes (in ~2h) -> upload traces (mira)
- kyle to push alloc-slab branch + microbench (today)
- ana to prototype comm-pool (tomorrow)
- dave to modify batcher bucketing thresholds + create eval harness (today)

kyle: I'll also add a small debug metric to the console: per-step temp-alloc-bytes and nccl-comm-bytes so we can correlate spikes to requests.

mira: thanks all. tagging @ana @dave for followups. will sync in the perf review tomorrow and decide which mitigations to ship to canary. :thumbsup:
